title: Child's cable mittens
subtitle: Full mittens for children with a simple 4-stitch cable panel on the back of the hand.
excerpt: Full mittens for children, worked in DK wool in the round, with a simple 4-stitch cable panel on the back of the hand and a 2x2 rib cuff. Afterthought thumb. Sized for children's hand circumferences of 14 and 16 cm.
sourceNotes: Child mittens with a cable panel. The construction follows a standard child mitten structure; the 4-stitch cable panel is adapted from published cable stitch collections.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts x 28 rounds = 10 x 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference CS 14 cm / CM 16 cm. Hand length CS 15 cm / CM 17 cm. For ages roughly 4-6 (CS) and 7-10 (CM).

glossaryTerms.definition: Slip 2 stitches to a cable needle and hold at the front of the work. Knit 2 stitches from the left needle, then knit the 2 stitches from the cable needle. This creates a left-leaning cable twist.

A thumb opening made by working the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the hand, then returning after the hand is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches which are picked up and worked as the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Full mittens for children, worked in DK wool in the round, with a simple
C4F
cable panel on the back of the hand and an
afterthought thumb
. Sized for children's hand circumferences of 14 cm (CS) and 16 cm (CM).
The cable crosses every 6 rounds over a 4-stitch panel, flanked by 2 purl stitches on each side. The back of the hand has the cable and the palm is plain stocking stitch. The construction uses
magic loop
on a long circular. Budget about 60 g (130 m / 142 yards) of DK wool per pair.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 60 g (about 130 m / 142 yards) of DK-weight wool

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Cable needle
items.qty: 1 small cable needle or bent stitch holder for the C4F cross

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 4: 1 for beginning of round, 2 for cable panel, 1 for top shaping midpoint

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 25 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for the afterthought thumb

content.text: Gauge
22 stitches and 28 rounds to 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles. The cable panel pulls in by about 1 stitch across 4 stitches; this is absorbed by the surrounding rib.
Cable panel

attrs.heading: Cable worked over 8 sts (p2, k4, p2)

items.name: Round 6 (cable cross)
items.qty: p2, C4F, p2. Repeat from round 1.

content.text: Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. CS = child small (14 cm circumference); CM = child medium (16 cm circumference).
Cast on and cuff
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 30 (36) stitches. Join to work in the round. Work 18 (20) rounds of 2x2 rib.
Set up cable panel

The cable panel sits at the centre of the back-of-hand half. Back: 15 (18) stitches. Palm: 15 (18) stitches. Centre the 8-stitch cable panel (p2, k4, p2) within the back half, with plain stocking stitch on either side.
Hand body

Work the 6-round cable repeat. After 2 (2) complete repeats (12 rounds), place the afterthought thumb: on the palm half, work the first 8 (9) palm stitches with waste yarn, slip back, and continue to end. Continue the cable for 2 (3) more repeats.
Top shaping

Place a marker at the midpoint. Decrease round: k1, ssk, knit to 3 before midpoint, k2tog, k1, SM, k1, ssk, knit to last 3, k2tog, k1. Plain round in stocking stitch. Repeat until 6 stitches remain. Draw yarn through and close.
Thumb
Remove waste yarn. Pick up 8 (9) stitches above and 8 (9) stitches below. Work 10 (12) rounds of 1x1 rib. Bind off in rib.
Common faults
Cable cross on the wrong round: the cross was worked on round 4 instead of round 6. Count every cable section from the last cross rather than from the cast-on.
Cable panel pulls in at the corners: the purl stitches flanking the cable were worked too tightly. Work each purl at the edge of the cable section with a slightly looser pull.
Finishing
Weave in all tails on the wrong side.
Care
Hand wash in cool water. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next
The same cable panel at adult size uses the same 6-round repeat and cable-needle technique. The cabled fingerless mitts pattern uses the same C4F cross at DK gauge.
